execution.timeout_scope: driver process, including any setup inside driver

protocol.architecture: 28-N-N-2 with two ReLU; middle bias absent in both arms
protocol.precision: FP32; TF32 disabled; existing FP64 geometry/Polar
protocol.normalization: all 10400000 training rows only; FP64 moments then FP32 application; FP32 statistics identical to historical HIGGS
protocol.initialization: stock radius CST and independently standard dense; ordinary layers/data order shared; no gain calibration

verification.cuda_binary_scope: compiled CUDA extension SHA/path is logged per CST cell; binary bytes were not retained and cannot be independently rehashed locally

limitations: Single-seed, one-epoch screening on a fixed validation subset; no test evaluation, uncertainty estimates, noninferiority or minimum-density claim. Dense and CST use different initializers. Learning rates selected on a short N1024 screen are reused across widths and densities.
Large-width dense quality drops with shared N1024-selected learning rate; width-specific tuning and sufficient training are required before any superiority/noninferiority claim.
Smaller CST currently has better AUC and lower cost than N8192; widening does not establish a task-quality advantage here.
Allocated/reserved are PyTorch allocator peaks, not total GPU process use.
Compiled CUDA binaries not retained; actual checkpoint/source/artifact bytes are retained.
